newsitem.title: USA: Dollar mixed in light pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar mixed in light pre-holiday trade.

text.p: The dollar drifted higher against the Japanese yen but fell against the German mark in quiet trading Friday as traders looked to lock in profits before the upcoming Christmas and New Year's holidays.

"People are not really too interested in giving up money," said James Powers, vice president at Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale in New York. "If they have had a good year they'll keep their money. If they had a bad year, why risk more? It is so close to the end of the year."
In very light trading, the dollar fell to 1.5515 marks from 1.5575 late on Thursday.
Meanwhile, a weak Japanese economy and sputtering stock market weighed on the yen, helping the dollar edge up to 114.27 yen late Friday from 114.03 yen late Thursday.

The market winds down early for Christmas and New Year's, and traders said they were setting holiday plans. For many, Friday was the last day before week-long vacations and many money trading centres are closed for at least two days over the next two weeks.
Christmas Day falls on Wednesday but markets in Germany are also shut Christmas Eve and the day after Christmas.

"Typically, it is a very illiquid time in our market these next two weeks," said Stephen Flanagan, vice president at Credit Agricole in New York. "I think people have done a lot of perhaps squaring up of positions."

Helping ensure the economy stays on the path to recovery, the Japanese government on Friday approved supplementary budget spending totalling 2.67 trillion yen ($23.4 billion) for the fiscal year ending March 31, 1997.

On Friday, the Nikkei 225 average, Japan's key stock index, did manage to regain some ground lost the day before, but the average still ended below the crucial 20,000 level which it punctured Thursday, making a low for the year.

But the dollar was unable to make much headway as Japanese investors reportedly needed to sell their U.S. bond holdings amid fears of a depreciation of the U.S. currency. Traders also said the yen's weakness against the dollar could take a toll on the already fragile stock market.

"It's a situation where a higher dollar/yen from this point on could have a negative implication for Nikkei stocks," said Jeffrey Yu, senior dealer at Sanwa Bank in New York. "Therefore, everybody's trading very cautiously about a higher dollar."
The dollar fell to 1.3345 Swiss francs from 1.3395 late Thursday. It rose to Canadian $1.3681 from C$1.3670.
The British pound rose to $1.6725 from $1.6647.
